clean_source_blocks.text: Rex Heuermann, known as the Gilgo Beach serial killer, who admitted to brutally murdering eight women, received the maximum sentence on Wednesday. He will serve three life sentences for first-degree murder, plus 25 years to life on four second-degree murder charges, all running consecutively. The sentencing followed a series of angry, poignant statements on Wednesday, as victims' family members described how the brutal losses created "lifelong devastation" for them. In April, Heuermann confirmed that he strangled and bound his victims before scattering their remains along Long Island's remote beaches. "You are a disgusting and despicable, small man, if you're a man at all. And you're a coward," said Judge Timothy Mazzei as he handed down the maximum sentence in a Riverhead, Long Island courtroom. "Get him out of here."
In fiery exchange, judge sentenced him to three life sentences plus 25 years to life on four other charges, all running consecutively.

Long Island serial killer Rex Heuermann has been sentenced to to multiple life sentences in prison without the possibility of parole after he pleaded guilty to killing seven women and admitted to killing an eighth. A Suffolk County, New York, judge handed Heuermann, 62, three consecutive life sentences, as well as an additional 100 years to life, on Wednesday, June 17 “All right, get him out of here,” the judge said as Heuermann was handcuffed and escorted out of the courtroom, according to CNN. Before his sentence was announced, several of his victims’ loved ones took the stand to address Heuermann. Amber Lynn Costello’s sister Ruth Ramos said she was comforted by the fact that her sibling’s killer will spend the rest of his life in prison.

See more of our coverage in your search results. Rex Heuermann was sentence to 3 life terms Wednesday after pleading guilty to the Gilgo Beach killings, which began nearly 30 years ago. A new mugshot of the psycho killer was released the day before his sentencing. Heuermann, 62, admitted in court in April that he strangled eight sex workers to death and dumped their bodies in desolate stretches of Long Island between 1993 and 2010. The plea deal came with a guaranteed sentence of three life terms, which were handed down in a Riverhead courthouse. Rex Heuermann, known as the Gilgo Beach serial killer, who admitted to brutally murdering eight women, received the maximum sentence on Wednesday.

He will serve three life sentences for first-degree murder, plus 25 years to life on four second-degree murder charges, all running consecutively.

The sentencing followed a series of angry, poignant statements on Wednesday, as victims' family members described how the brutal losses created "lifelong devastation" for them.

In April, Heuermann confirmed that he strangled and bound his victims before scattering their remains along Long Island's remote beaches.

"You are a disgusting and despicable, small man, if you're a man at all. And you're a coward," said Judge Timothy Mazzei as he handed down the maximum sentence in a Riverhead, Long Island courtroom. "Get him out of here."

Heuermann, who appeared in a dark suit, blue shirt and grey tie,  gave a brief statement before the sentence, claiming responsibility, then acknowledged that at this point, his words had "no meaning." When asked by the judge if he was "a little bit sorry", he replied, "yes".

The murders took place between 1993 and 2010, but the case took over a decade to solve.

After initially pleading not guilty, Heuermann ultimately admitted to the murders of: Melissa Barthelemy, 24; Megan Waterman, 22; and Amber Costello, 27; Maureen Brainard-Barnes, 25; Jessica Taylor, 20; Valerie Mack, 24; Sandra Costilla, 28; and Karen Vergata, 34.

After the hearing, Suffolk County District Attorney Ray Tierney gave credit to the families of the victims.  "I want them to get their revenge by going on to have wonderful lives…now it's time for them to heal," he said.

The hearing started with fiery statements from victims' family members.

Amanda, sister of Melissa Barthelemy, described to the court the phone calls Heuermann made to her family after killing her sister, detailing how he  was letting her sister's body "rot" and how he raped her. "I was 15," she said.

She addressed him directly:  "You can look at me when I'm talking to you. It's been 17 years since we last spoke."

For the first time, Heuermann, who had been staring  straight ahead blankly, turned  towards the podium, then immediately back.

Long Island serial killer Rex Heuermann has been sentenced to to multiple life sentences in prison without the possibility of parole after he pleaded guilty to killing seven women and admitted to killing an eighth.

Before his sentence was announced, several of his victims’ loved ones took the stand to address Heuermann.

Amber Lynn Costello’s sister Ruth Ramos said she was comforted by the fact that her sibling’s killer will spend the rest of his life in prison.

“While justice cannot bring [the victims] back, it ensures they are no longer forgotten and brings our families peace knowing the person responsible for our irreversible pain can never harm anyone else,” Ramos said, per CNN.

Heuermann, 62, was arrested for the killings in July 2023 and initially pleaded not guilty. However, he later pleaded guilty to the murders during a court appearance in April.

At the time, Heuermann told the judge that he killed Valerie Mack, Jessica Taylor, Megan Waterman, Melissa Barthelemy, Maureen Brainard-Barnes, Sandra Costilla, Amber Lynn Costello and Karen Vergata.

He made the admission as part of a plea deal and was expected to be handed three consecutive life sentences plus another 100 years. However, he did not learn his official sentencing until two months later on June 17.

The killings took place between 1993 and 2010 and all happened inside of his home with the exception of Costilla, who he said that he spontaneously killed in his car.

Heuermann’s crimes have garnered national attention and have been the subject of several documentaries. payload.title: Gilgo Beachin sarjamurhaaja tuomittiin elinkautisiin Long Islandilla
payload.summary: Rex Heuermann sai enimmäisrangaistuksen murhista, joihin hän oli myöntänyt syyllisyytensä tai osallisuutensa. Tuomio luettiin Suffolk Countyssa New Yorkissa.
payload.content:
Rex Heuermann, 62, on tuomittu useisiin peräkkäisiin elinkautisiin vankeusrangaistuksiin Long Islandilla New Yorkissa. Gilgo Beachin sarjamurhaajana tunnettu Heuermann oli myöntänyt tappaneensa seitsemän naista ja lisäksi tunnustanut kahdeksannen naisen surman. Tuomio annettiin keskiviikkona 17. kesäkuuta Riverheadin oikeustalossa Suffolk Countyssa.

## Enimmäisrangaistus useista murhista

Tuomari Timothy Mazzei määräsi Heuermannille kolme peräkkäistä elinkautista ensimmäisen asteen murhista. Lisäksi hän sai neljästä toisen asteen murhasyytteestä rangaistukset, jotka ovat 25 vuodesta elinkautiseen. Kaikki rangaistukset suoritetaan peräkkäin. Lähteiden mukaan tuomio vastasi enimmäisrangaistusta ja merkitsee, että Heuermann viettää loppuelämänsä vankilassa ilman mahdollisuutta päästä vapaaksi.

Heuermannin rikokset liitetään Gilgo Beachin murhiin, jotka ovat varjostaneet Long Islandia vuosikymmeniä. Oikeudessa esitettyjen tietojen mukaan hän myönsi huhtikuussa kuristaneensa uhrit, sitoneensa heidät ja jättäneensä heidän ruumiinsa syrjäisille ranta-alueille Long Islandilla. Tekojen kerrotaan tapahtuneen vuosien 1993 ja 2010 välillä.

## Uhrien omaiset puhuivat oikeudessa

Ennen tuomion julistamista useat uhrien läheiset puhuivat oikeudessa. He kuvasivat menetysten aiheuttaneen perheille pysyvää tuhoa ja surua, joka on jatkunut vuosien ajan. Amber Lynn Costellon sisar Ruth Ramos sanoi saavansa lohtua siitä, että hänen sisarensa tappaja joutuu viettämään loppuelämänsä vankilassa.

## Tuomari määräsi Heuermannin pois salista

Tuomion julistamisen yhteydessä oikeussalissa käytiin kireä sananvaihto. Tuomari Mazzei puhutteli Heuermannia poikkeuksellisen ankarasti ennen kuin määräsi hänet vietäväksi pois salista. Heuermann poistettiin oikeussalista käsiraudoissa tuomion jälkeen.

Tapaus on ollut yksi New Yorkin alueen seuratuimmista henkirikoskokonaisuuksista. Tuomio päättää keskeisen oikeusvaiheen asiassa, jossa uhrien omaiset ovat odottaneet vastauksia ja vastuuseen saattamista lähes kolmen vuosikymmenen ajan.
summary_bullets: Rex Heuermann tuomittiin useisiin peräkkäisiin elinkautisiin Long Islandilla.
Hän oli myöntänyt tappaneensa seitsemän naista ja tunnustanut kahdeksannen surman.
Uhrien omaiset kuvasivat oikeudessa rikosten aiheuttamaa pysyvää tuhoa.
